stem: An adult with sepsis has adequate source control and is clinically improving, but the optimal duration of antimicrobial therapy is unclear. Which use of procalcitonin is supported by the Surviving Sepsis Campaign?

options.A: Use procalcitonin together with clinical evaluation to help decide when to discontinue antimicrobials.
options.B: Use a single procalcitonin value to decide whether to start antimicrobials in suspected septic shock.
options.C: Use procalcitonin alone as definitive proof that the infection is bacterial.
options.D: Continue antimicrobials until procalcitonin is exactly zero regardless of the clinical course.

rationale: The Surviving Sepsis Campaign suggests using procalcitonin together with clinical evaluation to help decide when to discontinue antimicrobials in patients with sepsis or septic shock who have adequate source control when the optimal duration is unclear. It suggests against using procalcitonin plus clinical evaluation to decide when to start antimicrobials in suspected sepsis or septic shock.
educational_objective: Use procalcitonin appropriately as an adjunct to clinical evaluation in antimicrobial discontinuation decisions.
source_organization: Society of Critical Care Medicine / Surviving Sepsis Campaign
source_version_date: 2021 guideline; current SCCM guideline page accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Antimicrobial duration—procalcitonin plus clinical evaluation for discontinuation when duration unclear; suggest against PCT to decide initiation
source_claim_supported: Procalcitonin may supplement clinical evaluation when deciding when to discontinue antimicrobials in selected sepsis patients; it should not be used as a stand-alone start/stop diagnostic test.
correction_summary: Rejected the original oversimplification that procalcitonin is simply 'more specifically elevated in bacterial infection' and rebuilt around the guideline-supported clinical use.
audit_findings: Correct option tracks the guideline recommendation and its qualifying conditions.
Distractors misuse PCT as a stand-alone diagnostic or initiation rule.
Independent second pass found a unique best answer.
